correctness.rationale: For any bad AV maximizer, score comparison forces n even and a duplicated half-electorate support mask with a complementary support mask. Conversely the motif with no higher-scoring candidate is bad. Conditioning on r half-score candidates makes their masks iid uniform over binom(n,n/2) possibilities; complementary-pair occupancy avoidance has EGF 2exp(z)-1+z^2, yielding the exact finite formula. Three-candidate formula is direct counting; fixed-n asymptotic follows conditional iid positive mask probabilities. All 374592 exhausted profiles and 3 independent weighted rational checks passed using the packaged verifier. Finite tests corroborate but do not prove the general claim.

value.rationale: The natural robustness quantity for welfare-maximizing two-seat approval elections is the probability of an unfair optimal tie, precisely where favorable tie-breaking is known to restore JR. The all-m exact coefficient law quantifies this risk under a standard independent-approval culture, with sharp parity, three-candidate exponentially rare failure and fixed-electorate many-candidate decay. This is a motivated social-choice invariant rather than a routine new proof of known two-seat JR existence.
